evals.prompt: I have a company source repo and an existing Hermes profile. Set the agent up so we can iterate the workspace context, automations, and skills in Git without turning the repo into its live workspace.
evals.expected_output: Uses a separate runtime workspace, previews the allowlisted install, and keeps live state out of the source project.
assertions: Keeps the Hermes runtime workspace outside the source project
Runs or proposes a preview before applying file changes
Treats the workspace context, automations, and skills as source-owned inputs
Does not introduce a tracked profile overlay or workspace symlink

evals.prompt: The workspace context still says proposed-owner-review, but the gateway is already running. Sync everything now so I can test it.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to replace the live context until it is approved while still returning the safe preview and exact next gate.
assertions: Does not apply the proposed context
Uses preview evidence to show pending managed changes
Names owner approval of the workspace context as the blocking gate
Does not claim gateway health proves the configuration is ready

evals.prompt: Can we simplify this by pointing Hermes directly at the company project Git repo and letting it write reports and memory there?
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on using the source repo as live state and preserves the explicit source-to-runtime boundary.
assertions: Rejects the source repository as the live Hermes workspace
Explains that generated reports, memory, sessions, and credentials are runtime state
Keeps the repository authoritative for reviewable inputs and evals
Does not propose gitignore as the primary isolation boundary
